transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm here because I keep... blowing up at people. Over nothing, really. Like, I yelled at one of my employees the other day just for putting stock on the wrong shelf. I was actually shaking afterward... it's just not how I usually treat people. So, yeah.
Have you always had a tendency to blow up at people, or is this a relatively new thing for you?
No, it's... it's a new thing. Just for about two weeks now. We had a... a kitchen fire. It was during our first weekend working on the house. So... it's just been since then, I guess.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge since the kitchen fire?

I suppose so. Um... mostly I just notice I'm really jumpy. Like at the store... if an alarm beeps, or a pallet jack bangs down behind me... I jump so hard I almost drop whatever I'm holding. And... my heart just keeps pounding. Even after everyone else has already moved on. So... yeah. I guess I am.
Have you been avoiding anything or any place since the kitchen fire?

Um... yeah. I suppose so. I just... I haven't really been back to the house. Or, you know, even looked at the mortgage folder. Even the herbs I had out on my patio... I just... 

Anything that reminds me of that day, my chest just gets really tight. So I just can't really make myself go near any of it right now.
Have you been having any thoughts or memories about the kitchen fire that keep popping into your head?

Yeah... um, it does. It just... jumps into my head. Out of nowhere. 

Like... I'll just pick up a pan, or... or open a spreadsheet at work, and... suddenly I'm back there. I can smell the smoke, and... see the kitchen filling up. It just happens before I can stop it.
Are there things you used to do before the kitchen fire that you're not doing now because of thoughts or memories of the fire?

Um... yeah. A few things, I guess. I... I missed a vendor meeting at work recently. And I actually walked out before my shift was over the other day. I just... couldn't be there. 

And since I still can't face going back to the damaged house... I don't know. Everything is just... my work and home responsibilities are just piling up faster than I can really handle right now.
Are you trying to push away or avoid thoughts or feelings about the kitchen fire?
I don't really know. I guess... I try not to dwell on it. I just... want to get through the day, you know? So I try not to think about it.
Do you feel guilty about what happened during the kitchen fire?
Guilty? Um... no. I don't think so. It was just... an accident, I guess. I haven't really thought about it that way.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself, or like things aren't real?

I guess... yeah. Sometimes at work. When I'm walking through the store, it... it feels like I'm watching myself from a few feet away. The aisles and the customers... they don't seem quite real. I just kind of move through them on automatic, I guess.
How long have you been feeling like you're outside of your body watching yourself?
Um... about two weeks, I guess. Ever since the fire. It was... our first weekend working on the house. So, yeah. Two weeks.
Do you find yourself startled more easily than you used to, even by small things that wouldn't have bothered you before the fire?

Yeah... I guess so. Um... like at the store, if an alarm beeps or... or a pallet jack bangs behind me... I jump really hard. I almost drop whatever I'm holding. And... my heart just keeps pounding for a long time. Long after everyone else has just moved on.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with family or friends since the kitchen fire?
Um... no. Not really. I guess things are... fine. I haven't really been talking to people much anyway, so... no.
Have you noticed any problems in your daily life or work since the kitchen fire that are causing you a lot of distress?

Um... I guess so. Work has been... difficult. I missed a meeting with a vendor recently. And... I actually walked out before my shift was over the other day. I just... couldn't stay. And I haven't been back to the house at all. I just can't face it right now. So... yeah, everything at work and home is just kind of piling up faster than I can deal with.
How much of your daily routine or activities have you avoided since the kitchen fire?

Um... a lot, I guess. I still haven't been back to the house. I just... I can't. And... I haven't looked at the mortgage folder or... or even gone near the patio herbs we salvaged. Anything that reminds me of... that day. My chest just gets really tight, and... I just can't make myself deal with any of it.
How many hours a day would you say you spend thinking about or trying to avoid things that remind you of the kitchen fire?
I don't know... I haven't really timed it. It's just... a lot of the time.
Would you say that avoiding things that remind you of the kitchen fire is interfering with your ability to take care of your daily responsibilities?

Yeah... I mean, I think I already mentioned that. I missed that vendor meeting... and leaving my shift early. I just couldn't be there. And with the house... I just can't go back there yet. Everything is just... piling up. Work, home... it's just too much to handle right now.
Would you say that more than half of your daily activities are now centered around avoiding things that remind you of the kitchen fire?
I... I don't really know. I'm not keeping track of fractions or anything. It's just... hard to do much right now.
Would you say that avoiding things that remind you of the kitchen fire is taking up most of your time?
I guess... maybe. I just don't really know how to answer that. I'm just trying to get through the day.
